replication.target_description: Fonseca replication: sole critical Wilcoxon-Mann-Whitney comparison of three-person groups’ mean effort over rounds 1–5 between discriminating-reward 345COM and 345SUB treatments, identified in paragraphs 11–21.

es.location: Replication result, paragraph 21; critical-test definition, paragraphs 15–16
es.quote: We recorded an average effort level of 0.595 (s.d. 0.135) in the 345SUB treatment and an average effort level of 0.757 (s.d. 0.279) in the 345COM treatment. A Wilcoxon-Mann-Whitney test yielded a significant difference: exact p=0.018.

reported_success.location: Replication criterion, paragraphs 15–16; Replication result, paragraphs 19–21
reported_success.quote: We recorded an average effort level of 0.595 (s.d. 0.135) in the 345SUB treatment and an average effort level of 0.757 (s.d. 0.279) in the 345COM treatment. A Wilcoxon-Mann-Whitney test yielded a significant difference: exact p=0.018.

notes: Identity assessment: paragraph 1 identifies a replication of Goerg et al. (2010), Journal of Labor Economics; paragraph 3 names Miguel A. Fonseca; paragraph 6 gives Project ID Goerg_JournLabEco_2010_WLpV_1964; paragraph 7 gives OSF project https://osf.io/t9h6p/. Source line identifies download fgdxs. These match the supplied neutral replication reference/project and URL. This is a primary completed replication report, with results, deviations, materials, analysis instructions and original citation, rather than merely a preregistration or abstract. Listed reference coauthors and reference date are not independently printed in the text. No PDF supplied. The critical comparison is explicitly identified by claim, treatments, rounds and analysis unit; no mapping by input order or numeric matching. Paragraph 21 reports treatment means, standard deviations and exact p=0.018, but no rank-biserial effect size, standardized effect, or W/U statistic. No effect conversion performed. The authors describe a significant difference but give no explicit replication-success verdict; success left null under the authors-narrative-verdict rule rather than inferred from significance. Only es_value_r and reported_success are assigned; original and unassigned n/p fields are placeholders, not extraction findings.
